name: Preamble — Extension of Collective Bargaining Agreement
text: This Memorandum of Agreement made and entered into by and between The New York Times Company ("The Times") and the Newspaper and Mail Deliverers' Union of New York and Vicinity ("union") shall extend the current Collective Bargaining Agreement, which expires on March 30, 1993, until March 30, 2000 to the extent such Collective Bargaining Agreement is not modified by, or inconsistent with, the terms and conditions set forth herein.

name: 1.A. Contract applicable at new or rebuilt facilities
text: A. Except as otherwise provided herein, the contract | as modified by this Memorandum shall have full force and effect at any new or rebuilt facility operated by The Times within the territorial jurisdiction of the NMDU.

name: 1.B. Edison innovations may be employed elsewhere
text: B. The parties agree that the technological innovations, methods of operation, scheduling practices and/or working conditions to be employed at Edison, e.g. palletization, tractor-trailer delivery to wholesalers, and card reader system, may also be employed at any new or rebuilt facility to be operated -y The Times.

name: 1.C. Further innovations; interest arbitration
text: c. The parties acknowledge that The Times may, at a new or rebuilt facility, seek to employ further technological innovations, methods of operation, scheduling practices, and/or working conditions FUNDO0001099 different from and/or in addition to those employed at Edison. In that event, and in the event that after a period of 120 days, the parties are unable through negotiation to resolve any disputes over such matters, the parties agree to submit the disputes to final and binding interest arbitration before the Merits Arbitrator.

name: 2. The Contract Arbitrator — termination and duties of Merits Arbitrator
text: Either party may, within the sixty (60) day period preceding March 30 of each contract year, terminate the incumbent "Merits Arbitrator", with the termination to become effective upon the selection by the parties, pursuant to the procedure set forth below, of a new "Merits Arbitrator". The Merits Arbitrator shall, except _ as otherwise provided herein, be responsible for hearing and resolving all grievances, differences and disputes initiated after his selection that arise out of the interpretation or application of the Agreement at all facilities operated by. The Times within the territorial jurisdiction of the NMDU.

name: 2. Selection of replacement Merits Arbitrator
text: In the event that either party exercises its right as described above to terminate the Merits Arbitrator, and in the event that the parties fail to reach agreement on a new Merits Arbitrator, the Merits Arbitrator shall be selected pursuant to the Voluntary Labor Arbitration Rules of the American Arbitration Association.

name: 2. Termination of Status Quo Arbitrator
text: Either party may, within the sixty (60) day period preceding September 30 of each contract year, terminate the incumbent Status Quo Arbitrator. Said termination shall become effective upon the selection by the parties of a new Status Quo Arbitrator pursuant to the procedure described in paragraph B above.

name: 3.A. Buyout offer
text: In order to effectuate necessary manning reductions at Edison in the nost fair and. equitable manner, The Times will offer a voluntary buyout to all active NMDU RSHs employed by the Times, including foremen, and to all active "Eligible Group I Employees," as defined below. The buyout offer will be in accordance with the terms and conditions as set forth in Attachments A 4 FUNDOO001101 and B attached hereto and made part hereof. The following summarizes the elements of the offer:

name: 3.A.1) $70,000 to RSHs
text: The amount of $70,000 will be offered to all active NMDU RSHs in the form of lump sum payments or annuities.

name: 3.A.2) $35,000 to Eligible Group I Employees
text: The amount of $35,000 will be offered to all active "Eligible Group I Employees" in the form of lump sum payments or annuities. For purposes of this Agreement, "Eligible Group I Employees" shall mean individuals included on the Times Group I list as of the date of signing of this Agreement who are still on the Group I list on the date of ratification.

name: 3.A.3) Health and welfare contributions 1992-1995
text: For the calendar years 1992, 1993, 1994, and 1995, The Times will make health and welfare contributions to the NMDU Health and Welfare Fund for a minimum of 450 Full Time Equivalents. For purposes of this Agreement, 260 shifts per year shall constitute one Full Time Equivalent. The contributions shall be based on the highest straight time scale applicable for the contract year in which the contributions are made. It is understood 5 FUNDO001 102 5) that these contributions shall be in lieu of and not in addition to those that would otherwise be called for by the Agreement.

name: 3.A.4) One-time health and welfare contributions
text: Upon termination of the buyout offer, and upon severance from the payroll of those accepting the buyout, The Times will make a one-time contribution to the NMDU Health and Welfare Fund which will be equal to fifteen thousand dollars ($15,000) multiplied by the number of active NMDU RSHs who take the buyout. In addition, The Times will make a one-time contribution to the NMDU Health and Welfare Fund which will be equal to seven thousand five hundred dollars ($7,500) multiplied by the number of active Eligible Group I Employees who take the buyout.

name: 3.A.5) Pension contributions for RSHs accepting buyout
text: The Times will make pension contributions to the NMDU Pension Fund on behalf of RSHs who accept the buyout, to age 65 or for a period of five (5) years, whichever comes first. The contributions shall be based on the highest straight time scale applicable for the contract year in which the contributions are made.

name: 3.A.6) Life insurance continuation
text: 6) The Times life insurance will be continued on behalf of RSHs that accept the buyout, to age 65 or for 5 years, whichever comes first.

name: 3.A.7) Buyout offer open 45 days
text: 7) The buyout offer will remain open for a period of 45 days commencing promptly after ratification of this Agreement.

name: 4.A. Additions to RSH list
text: Upon termination of the buyout offer, and upon severance from the payroll of those accepting the buyout, The Times will add to the RSH list the number of employees necessary to reach 370 regular situations. Such additions to the list shall come from the Eligible Group I Employees who do not accept the buyout.

name: 4.B. Replacement procedure for Eligible Group I Employees
text: tligible Group I Employees who do not become RSHs as a result of the procedure described in paragraph A shall, during the term of this Agreement, and up to a maximum of 370, replace, on a one-for-one basis, RSHs who cease to be employees of the Times for any reason, e.g., death, retirement, resignation, discharge, etc. This replacement procedure shall apply only to FUNDO001 104 Eligible Group I Employees as defined above. Eligible Group I Employees who become RSHs as a er result of this replacement procedure shall have a length of contract employment guarantee governed by the terms of Appendix A. Once the replacement procedure has been completed, there shall be no [oo less than 270 RSHS during the term of this Agreement.

name: 4.C. No daily replacement of absent RSHs
text: Cc. Once the procedure described in paragraph A is completed, The Times will not be required to replace on a daily, nightly, or weekly basis RSHs who are scheduled to work at any facility, but are absent for any reason, e.g. illness, vacation, jury duty, personal day, etc., unless the total number of RSHs who report to work is insufficient to satisfy specific manning requirements.

name: 4.D. Vacated situations; consolidation of segments
text: D. In the ‘ever.c that a regular situation is vacated after the procedure described in paragraph A is completed, either because a RSH ceases to be an employee of The Times for any reason, e.g., death, retirement, resignation, discharge, etc., or : because the RSH bids off the job: (i) an employee | need not be promoted to the status of RSH unless necessary to comply either with the replacement FUNDO001105 precedure set forth in paragraph B above or with specific manning requirements; and (ii) following discussion with the Union, the vacated situation may be filled or eliminated at the discretion of The Times, unless the situation must be filled to comply with specific manning requirements. As attrition below 370 RSHs occurs, The Times shall also have the right to consolidate segments of vacated situations into corresponding "open" segments of the existing bid work schedules of other RSH’s, provided that the RSH’s with the corresponding "open'! segments will be permitted to bid by seniority on the segments to be consolidated. In the event there are no bidders, the segments will be assigned to the junior of such RSH’s. It is further provided that The Times may not so consolidate vacated situations in which one run constitutes the entire day’s or night’s work for a shift on three or more shifts each week.

name: 5. West Side Direct Reorganization
text: 5. West Side Direct Reorganization Immediately following the closure of the forty-five (45) day buyout offer peried, the Times shall have the right to consolidate and otherwise reorganize all 9 FUNDO0001106 existing daily West Side Direct routes, including both daily and Sunday routes. A reduction of fifty percent ‘ee (50%) of the existing daily West Side Direct routes : will be permitted in this reorganization. As a result of that reduction, there will be thirteen (13) daily West Side Direct routes, and thirteen (13) chauffeur and sixteen (16) tailmen assignments will remain. With respect to the Sunday West Side Direct routes, there will be twelve (12) routes carrying Sunday Main and Sports. As a result of this reduction, twelve (12) chauffeurs and twelve (12) tailmen will remain.

name: 6. Bulldog Reorganization — SNBD route consolidation
text: 6. Bulldog Reorganization a~ Immediately following the closure of the forty-five (45) day buyout offer period, The Times shall have the right to consolidate and otherwise reorganize all existing Saturday Night Bulldeg (SNBD) routes. The routes may deliver the four-she c (Package 3 when Edison opens) and the Sunday Main and Sports together. The reorganization shall be subject only to the limitation that the minimum number of all SNBD routes on Saturday evening shall be forty (40). Relay cars and flash cars will be used based on the needs of the 10 J ee TEN\FSS\WPSI\FIRM\OSS7\50000.FS5 55553-062 #T21P (386) 05/16/92 5: 16pm FUNDO001107 operation, provided that there shall be a minimum of two (2) flash cars. As a result of the reduction in SNBD routes, forty (40) chauffeur and forty-eight (48) tailmen assignments will remain.

name: 6. SNBD starting times after Edison
text: After the commencement of operations at Edison, the starting times for chauffeurs and tailmen on SNBD routes will be no later than 4:00 p.m.

name: 6. Daily Bulldog route reorganization
text: The Times also shall have the right to consolidate and otherwise reorganize daily Bulldog routes down to a minimum of two routes on Sunday nights and four routes on Monday - Friday nights.

name: 6. Elimination of cash collections
text: All cash collections on daily Bulldog and SNBD accounts shall be eliminated, and the Company will be permitted to institute an alternate billing system. Cash collections will continue on recovery routes.

name: 7.A. No strikes
text: No Strikes/No Lockouts A. There shall be no strikes (including, but not limited to, sympathy strikes), job actions, any acts honoring a picket line against the publisher or any of its wholesalers, newsdealers, T<-Route _ contractors, home delivery or vending machine ii FUNDO0001 108 dealers, or any other acts that interfere with the Publisher’s operations or the production or sale of its products or services, during the term of this Agreement by the Union, its officers, agents and members, or by the employees represented by the Union. The Union agrees that it will not authorize, ratify or condone any strike or any other activity described herein and further agrees that the Union, its officers and agents, will act as expeditiously as possible to do everything lawful within their power to prevent a violation of this provision and to stop a violation if it has occurred, including, but not limited to, immediately notifying members, officers and agents of the Union that conduct or anticipated conduct in violation of this provision is illegal and in violation of the Agreement.

name: 7.B. No lockouts
text: B. The Publisher agrees that there will be no lockeut of employees during the term of the Agreement.

name: 7.C. Release from no strike-no lockout provision
text: Cc. Upon the failure of either party to comply with a decision, award or order of the Joint Standing Committee, the Adjustment Board or the Appeal Board, the other party, after five (5) working days, shall be released from the "no strike-no 12 FUNDO0001109 lockout" provision as the case may be, provided that the party seeking release from this "no : Se strike-no lockout provision" first obtains a determination from the issuing neutral tribunal that there has been no substantial compliance with the award and further provided that the noncomplying party within that five (5) day period has not filed a motion, petition or other action to modify, clarify or vacate said decision, award or order.

name: 8.A. Existing wages through March 30, 1993
text: 8. Wages Applicable To All Facilities A. Wages established under the current Collective f~ Bargaining Agreement shall remain in effect through March 30, 1993.

name: 8.B. Wage increase effective March 31, 1993
text: B. Wage increases subsequent to March 30, 1993 will be as set: forth below: 0 Effective March 31, 1993, the weekly journeyman day scale shall be increased by $36.00 per week and will result in a weekly journeyman day scale of $952.80

name: 8.B. Wage increase effective March 31, 1994
text: fe) Effective March 31, 1994, the weekly journeyman day scale shall be increased by $34.00 per week and will result in a weekly journeyman day scale of $986.80.

name: 8.B. Wage increase effective March 31, 1995
text: Effective March 31, 1995, the weekly journeyman day scale shall be increased by $34.00 per week and will result in a weekly journeyman day scale of $1020.80.

name: 8. Wage reopener for 1996-2000
text: Within ninety (90) days prior to March 31, 1996, the parties will meet for the purpose of negotiating wage rates for the period March 31, 1996 through March 30, 2000. If the parties are unable to reach agreement within thirty (30) days after the commencement of bargaining under the reopener, the matter will be submitted to binding arbitration. Wage givebacks below the then current scale will not be a proper subject for consideration by the arbitrator.

name: 8. Reapportionment of pension and welfare contributions
text: With respect to wage increases effective March 31, 1993 and thereafter, the Union may elect to reapportion the contributions due on those increases between its pension plan and its health and welfare plan the total pension (8%) and health 14 FUNDOO01111 and welfare (7.68%) plan contributions made by The Times, provided that: (1) the total contribution made by The Times to all plans does not exceed 15.68%; (ii) the Union notifies The Times at least ninety (90) days in advance of its intent to reapportion the contributions; and (iii) the reapportionment shall not, in any event, result in a contribution to the pension fund of less then the amount necessary to meet any minimum contribution requirements established by law.

name: 8. Cost of living adjustments
text: Cost of living adjustments pursuant to the relevant provisions of the Contract shall be made effective March 31, 1994, March 31, 1995, March 31, 1997, March 31, 1998, March 31, 1999, provided that all such adjustments beginning on March 31, 1992 shall utilize a January to January rather than a May to May Index.

name: 9. Ratification
text: 9. It is understood and agreed that this Memorandum of Agreement is subject to ratification by each of the parties hereto.

name: Attachment A, I.1) Eligibility
text: Eligibility 1) Applies to active NMDU regular situation holders (RSHs) on The New York Times Steady Situation list, including foremen, currently holding positions at The Times.

name: Attachment A, II.1) Buyout payment amount
text: Schedule of Payments 1) The buyout payment for eligible employees shall be $70,000.

name: Attachment A, II.2) Lump sum or annuity
text: 2) The buyout amount set forth in Paragraph 1 above shall be paid in a lump sum, unless the RSH electing to leave requests, in writing, that The Times purchase an annuity. The Times will purchase an annuity through a major insurance carrier, should such a request be made. Any annuity purchase will include interest at prevailing market interest rates.

name: Attachment A, II.3) Death before full payment
text: 3) If an employee who has elected and is qualified for a buyout dies prior to receiving the entire FUNDOO001114 4) amount to which he or she is entitled with respect to the buyout, the unpaid balance will be paid to the employee’s estate. In the event that an employee should choose an annuity, the terms of the annuity will apply.

name: Attachment A, II.4) Unemployment compensation claims
text: The Times will not oppose claims for unemployment compensation made by individuals accepting the buyout.

name: Attachment A, III.1) Pension and welfare contributions
text: The Times will make contributions to the Pension and Welfare Funds as specified in Paragraph 3-A- (3) and 3-A-(5} of the Memorandum of Agreement.

name: Attachment A, III.2) Life insurance continuation
text: The Times’ life insurance will be continued on behalf of RSHs that accept the buyout, to age 65 or for five (5) years, whichever comes first.

name: Attachment A, III.3) Notice of Termination requirement
text: An employee who elects to accept the buyout must notify The Times in writing by completing the attached Notice of Termination that he or she is voluntarily surrendering his or her contractual guarantee of employment in return for a buyout.

name: Attachment A, III.4) Buyout offer period
text: 4) The buyout offer will remain open for a period of 45 days commencing promptly after ratification of this Agreement.

name: Attachment B, I.1) Eligibility
text: Eligibility 1) Applies to active "Eligible Group I List Employees" who are on said list effective the date of ratification of this Memorandum of Agreement.

name: Attachment B, II.1) Buyout payment amount
text: The buyout payment for eligible employees shall be $35,000.

name: Attachment B, II.2) Lump sum or annuity
text: The buyout amount set forth in Paragraph 1 above shall be paid in a lump sum, unless the individual electing to leave requests, in writing, that The | Times purchase an annucy. The Times will purchase an annuity through a major insurance carrier, should such a request be made. Any annuity purchase will include interest at prevailing market interest rates.

name: Attachment B, II.3) Death before full payment
text: If an individual who has elected and is qualified for a buyout dies prior to receiving the entire amount to which he or she is entitled with respect FUNDO001118 5) to the buyout, the unpaid balance will be paid to the individual’s estate. In the event that an individual should choose an annuity, the terms of the annuity will apply.

name: Attachment B, II.4) Unemployment compensation claims
text: The Times will not oppose claims for unemployment compensation made by individuals accepting the buyout.

name: Attachment B, II.5) Buyout offer period
text: The buyout offer will remain open for a period of 45 days commencing promptly after ratification of this Agreement.

name: Appendix A, A. Guaranteed Employees
text: A. Guaranteed Employees Employees eligible for guaranteed employment ("Guaranteed Employees") are those Regular Situation Holders to be identified on Attachments "1" and "2",

name: Appendix A, B. Guarantees
text: B. Guarantees Guaranteed Employees as identified on Attachments "1" and "2" will be guaranteed the opportunity to work five straight time shifts per week for the duration of their guarantee period.

name: Appendix A, B. Effectiveness of guarantees
text: The employment guarantees of this Agreement provided to 4 each employee named in Attachments "1" and "2" as described above shall become effective upon completion of the process described in paragraph 4B of the Memorandum of Agreement and remain in éffect as follows:

name: Appendix A, B.1. Guarantees for Attachment "1" employees
text: 1. Employment guarantees for those employees named +n Attachment "1" shall remain in full force and effect for as long as any named employee is employed by The New York Times .in a position that is within the scope of the present NMDU bargaining unit. This provision shall survive the expiration of this Agreement.

name: Appendix A, B.2. Guarantees for Attachment "2" employees
text: 2s Employment guarantees for those employees named in Attachment "2" shall remain in full force and effect for as long as any named employee remains a member of the bargaining unit and in the employ of Ts\FSS\WPST\FIRM\OSE7\50000.FS5 55553-0862 WT21P (386) 05/16/92 5:16pm FUNDOO001121 The New York Times, but said guarantee shall continue enly until the expiration date of the current Collective Bargaining Agreement.

name: Appendix A, C. Utilization
text: Cc. Utilization The Times shall have the right to utilize fully the services of Guaranteed Employetés before employing any additional employees with the understanding that utilization of such employees will be done in inverse seniority order.

name: Appendix A, D. General
text: D. General The employment guarantees set forth above shall apply only to those individuals listed in Attachments "1" and "2" and shall not be transferable or otherwise applicable to any other individuals, except for Eligible Group I Employees who obtain guarantees pursuant to paragraph 4B of the Memorandum of ; Agreement.

name: Appendix A, E. Duration — suspension of operations
text: E. ,. Duration The guarantee set forth above will be suspended in the event that the delivery department’s operations are suspended in circumstances under which RSH’s are not entitled to be paid under the Collective Bargaining Agreement.

name: Appendix A, E. Permanent suspension of the Newspaper
text: In the event of a permanent suspension of the Newspaper, the employment guarantees of this Agreement shall cease.

name: Appendix A, E. Terminated employees
text: Employment guarantees shall not apply to any employee who terminates employment for any reason, including but not limited to, retirement, resignation, discharge, Geath and permanent disability.

name: Appendix A, E. No-Strike consideration; termination of guarantees
text: In consideration for the guarantee herein, the Union reaffirms its commitment to the No~Strike clause contained in this Memorandum of Agreement. In the event of any violation of that No-Strike clause, and in the event that the violation continues notwithstanding the issuance of a temporary restraining order by a FUNDO001122 court after a hearing, the guarantees set forth herein may be terminated at the option of The Times.

name: Side letter — Me-too wage package option
text: This will confirm the understanding reached between the parties in the recent contract negotiations. If, in connection with any collective bargaining agreement, letter agreement, side agreement or memoranda of agreement now effective or which later becomes effective through and including March 30, 2000 or any shorter period, The Times agrees with any labor organization (Electricians, Guild, Machinists, Mailers, Paperhandlers, Photo~Engravers, Pressmen, Stereotypers, Typographers) representing The Times’s employees upon a wage package which is additional to or different from that contained herein, the Union may, at its option, adopt such increased wage package provided that such increased wages have not been granted in exchange for productivity improvements or attrition exceeding that which is contained in The New York Times/NMDU Memorandum of Agreement, or have not been diverted from an existing or subsequently negotiated wage package. Any dispute about the application of this paragraph shall be resolved through the Contract’s grievance and arbitration procedure.

name: Side letter — Vacating the Preliminary Injunction
text: This will confirm our understanding reached during recent negotiations with respect to vacating the Preliminary Injunction granted on March 28, 1992. As agreed, The Times will file the necessary papers to vacate the preliminary injunction promptly upon notification by the NMDU of ratification of the Memorandum of Agreement dated May 16, 1992.

name: Side letter — New and rebuilt facilities exclusion
text: This will confirm our discussions during recent negotiations concerning Section 1, New and Rebuilt Facilities of the Memorandum of Agreement dated May 16, 1992. It is agreed that all references to "new and rebuilt facilities". contained within the Memorandum of Agreement will not apply to the 43rd Street and/or the staging facility.

name: Side letter — Saturday Night Bulldog finishing times
text: Pursuant to discussions conducted during the recent contract negotiations, it is understood and agreed that after the consolidation of the Saturday Night Bulldog routes as contemplated by paragraph 6 of our May 16, 1992 Agreement, forty (40) of the current Satuday Night Bulldog finishing times will be assigned to the forty (40) remaining routes, and those finishing times will remain unchanged throughout the duration of this contract.

name: Side letter — Welfare Fund shortfalls for Eligible Group I Employees
text: With respect to the Welfare Fund, the parties agree that any shortfalls that may exist between shift contributions needed to maintain benefits status for the Eligible Group I Employees referred to above, and the shift contributions made based on such individuals’ actual employment by The Times, will be funded by contributions made pursuant to paragraph 3.A.(3) of the Memorandum. Te the extent the contributions provided for in paragraph 3.A.(3) oi the Memorandum are insufficient to cover such shortfalls, The Times will make the additional contributions to the Welfare Funeé that are necessary to maintain benefit status.

name: Side letter — Pension Fund shortfalls
text: With respect to the Pension Fund, the parties agree that separate contributions will be made by The Times to fund any shortfalls that may exist between shift contributions needed to maintain benefit status for the Eligible Group I Employees referred to above, and the shift contributions made based on such individuals’ actual employment by The Times.

name: Side letter — Condition on funding shortfalls
text: It is understood that The Times’s obligation to fund the shortfalls, as described above, is conditioned on the willingness of the individuals involved to avail themselves of all work opportunities that may exist at The New York Times.

name: Side letter — Increase in minimum FTE contributions
text: This will confirm our discussions during recent negotiations concerning contributions to the NMDU Health and Welfare Fund pursuant to paragraph 3-A(3) of the Memorandum of Agreement. As agreed, during the period between the ratification of the Memorandum of Agreement and the full oo commencement of operations at Edison, to the extent the number of full-time equivalents (FTE’s) employed by The Times exceeds 370, the minimum number of FTE contributions to the Health and Welfare Fund, as provided for in paragraph 3-A(3) of the Memorandum of Agreement, will be increased by a number equal to the number of FTE’s employed in excess of 370.

name: Side letter — Schools and Colleges program
text: This will confirm our discussions in recent negotiations with respect to the establishment of a Schools and Colleges program. As agreed, School and College accounts will continue to be integrated into direct delivery routes that alse serve other types of outlets. Dedicated school and college routes may be added as needed. Drivers for these dedicated routes will be assigned to a regular shift time of 2:30 to 9:30 a.n. The Times may require deliveries to be made at specified times to specified locations within the schools or colleges. Such routes may be suspended, e.g., during summer and school holidays, or abolished at the discretion of The Times, and the driver’s start time will revert to 11:30 p.m. Such routes will not require a tailman.

name: Side letter — Bootlegging operations
text: This will confirm our discussions in recent negotiations with respect to the NMDU’s concerns regarding "hootlegging" operations. The New York Times will make every effort within its control to insure that the NMDU’s jurisdiction with respect to the delivery of newspapers, as provided for in the Collective Bargaining Agreement, is protected against ( "hootlegging" operations.

name: Side letter — Carlstadt/Edison transition committee establishment
text: This will confirm our discussions during recent negotiations concerning the establishment of a Carlistadt/Edison transition committee, to address issues which arise from the transfer of the appropriate workforce from Carlstadt to Edison and Carlstadt to 43rd Street. As agreed, within thirty (30) days after ratification of the Memorandum of Agreement, The Times and a the Union shall establish a committee comprised of two Times is representatives and two Union representatives.

name: Side letter — Charge of transition committee
text: The committee will be specifically charged with administering the transfer process of employees from Carlstadt to Edison and Carlstadt to 43rd Street.

name: Side letter — 1996 H&W contributions for buyout employees age 60 or below
text: This will confirm the understanding reached between the parties with respect to contributions to the Health and Welfare Fund for employees who take the buyout and who,will be age sixty (60) or below at the time they terminate their employment with The New York Times. The parties agree that The Times will make contributions to the Health and Welfare Fund on behalf of such employees for the calendar year 1996. It is further agreed that the contributions to the NMDU Health and Welfare Fund agreed to in the Memorandum of Agreement, i.e., annual shift contributions based on 450 Full Time Equivalents, will be reduced by the number of Health and Welfare shift contributions made in 1996 on behalf of employees who take the buyout and. are age sixty (60) or below on the date they terminate their employment via the buyout. Said reductions will be evenly distributed throughout the calendar years 1992, 1993, 1994, and 1995.

name: Side letter — Amendments to Health and Welfare Plan
text: The parties mutually agree to take the steps necessary to effectuate amendments to the Health and Welfare Plan necessitated to implement the contributions to the Health and Welfare Fund agreed to in paragraph 3-A(3) of the Memorandum of Agreement and this letter.

name: Side letter — Filling vacant, newly created or temporary situations
text: This will confirm our understanding reached during recent negotiations regarding the necessity to expeditiously staff vacant, newly created, or temporary situations. As agreed, in the event a need should arise to fill any such situations at Edison, The Times and the Union agree, on an inverse seniority basis, to assign the most junior qualified situation holder to that situation pending final award or, in the case of temporary situations, termination of the situation.

name: Side letter — Notice to junior situation holders
text: Junior situation holders assigned in accordance with the above shall be given no less than four (4) days’ notice prior to such assignment. At the conclusion of a temporary situation, they shall be restored to their former situation. They shall be permanently assigned to permanent or vacant positions in the event those situations are not filled by bid.

name: Side letter — Chapel Chairman notification procedure
text: Prior to instituting the procedure above, The Times shall notify the Chapel Chairman of the vacancy. The Chapel Chairman will, within three (3) days of such notification, supply the name of a situation holder who wishes to voluntarily accept the situation at Edison to The Times. Such situation holders shall fill the situation within seven (7) days from the date of the above notification to the Chapel Chairman. In the event the situation is not filled by bid, the most junior qualified situation holder will be permanently assigned to the vacancy and the volunteer shall return to his regular situation.

name: Side letter — Exclusion for short temporary vacancies
text: The above procedures shall not be applied to any temporary vacancy which is foreseen to be of two (2) weeks or less duration.

name: Side letter — Option to fill resulting vacancies
text: The Times shall have the option to fill any vacancies created as a result of the assignment of a junior situation holder assigned in accordance with this letter.

name: Side letter — Closure of Daily News or Post
text: This will confirm our discussions during recent negotiations with respect to the Union’s concern regarding the possible closure of either the New York Daily News or the New York Post. In the event that either of the above-referenced newspapers permanently ceases operations, the NMDU may, within 72 hours, discuss the possibility of employment opportunities at The New York Times of impacted employees.

name: Side letter — M. Santor grievance settlement (position awarded)
text: This will confirm an understanding reached during recent negotiations with respect to the settlement of M. Santor’s outstanding grievance. As agreed, M. Santor will be awarded the position ; of Dispatcher, Sunday through Thursday, with Friday/Saturday ~ days off. The start time of the position will be 5:00 p.m.

name: Side letter — M. Santor withdrawal of grievance
text: It is further agreed that M. Santor, in consideration of this agreement, will withdraw his grievance with prejudice.
